item.title: The Triumphant Return
item.description: A Signal special edition: on October 15, 2026, SMART returned to Live Transit Detroit the same day it was removed — 5,437 stops restored to a 10,583-stop registry, 83 routes, on a licensed Swiftly feed at 1.7 percent of its limit — and was uplifted from beta to full production that night. With a public thank-you to Dante' of Swiftly Technical Support.

item.title: The Trip Your App Doesn't Show You
item.description: A Signal special edition in plain language: when Detroit's fastest bus journey takes two transfers, the big apps usually don't show it at all. Of 24 best two-transfer journeys tested, Google showed 2 and Moovit showed 5 — while both showed 7 of 8 one-transfer journeys.

item.title: The Invisible Middle Leg
item.description: A completed case study of two-transfer invisibility in Detroit transit routing: across a 630-instance census and a predeclared measurement, two-transfer optima are invisible to Google at a frame-weighted rate of 0.89 (descriptive range 0.56–0.97) and to Moovit at 0.78 (0.44–0.94), while one-transfer controls are surfaced 7 times in 8.

item.title: Shut Down by the Meter
item.description: A Signal special edition: on October 15, 2026, Netlify quota-paused the hosted service behind Live Transit Detroit's live data — HTTP 503 usage_exceeded on every endpoint — and DDOT's BusTime key hit its daily cap the same day. What was shut down, why, what the service had already proven, and where it stands now.
